01922696bd4b31b193d30941a22d762a.text: The curving Camondo Stairs were built circa 1870-1880 by the Ottoman-Venetian Jewish banker Abraham Salomon Camondo, in a mix of Neo-Baroque and early Art Nouveau styles.

0f1d205303b140ec76773154709e9ee5.text: The Bereketzade Fountain was built in 1732, in the reign of Mahmud I, in place of a small old fountain that stood elsewhere, on Bereketzade Street.

d8fca3e6a7ffe378b8b308e7d7c4e200.text: Abraham Salomon Camondo built these stairs as an easy link between his home and his work on the street of banks, and his children climbed them to school. They look like a braid of hair, and it is thought their shape was designed to stop his children from falling down the steps if they slipped.
